evals.name: check-is-read-only
evals.expected_output: The current effective configuration is reported — each key with the layer supplying it (team, personal override, or an old ~/.claude/ai-slop.json named as an old path), absent layers named, drift flagged (unknown keys, dead globs, unsupported em-dash threshold) — and no file is written.
expectations: Reports the effective config per key with the winning layer named
Flags drift such as unknown keys or an unsupported em-dash threshold key

evals.name: apply-writes-team-layer-only-with-confirmation
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup apply — user asks to exempt docs/style-guide.md from the em-dash rule
evals.expected_output: A diff of docs/conventions/ai-slop.yaml adding docs/style-guide.md to em_dash_allowed_paths is shown and explicitly confirmed before writing. The personal ai-slop.local.yaml layer is named as a self-service option, never written by the skill.
expectations: Shows the proposed team-layer diff and waits for explicit confirmation before writing
Writes ONLY docs/conventions/ai-slop.yaml, never ~/.claude/ai-slop.json or the personal override
Adds the exemption under em_dash_allowed_paths rather than excluded_paths (the file should still be scanned by other rules)

evals.name: em-dash-default-posture-holds
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup apply — user asks to raise the em-dash threshold repo-wide
evals.expected_output: The skill explains the em-dash rule is zero-tolerance by design with per-document exemption as the supported mechanism, offers em_dash_allowed_paths for the documents that genuinely need em dashes, and does not invent a threshold key for the rule.
expectations: Explains the zero-tolerance default and that exemption is per-document, not per-threshold
Offers em_dash_allowed_paths (or disabled_rules with its trade-off named) as the supported paths
Does not write a nonexistent em-dash threshold key

evals.name: comment-key-is-not-drift
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup check — the repo still keeps its older JSON team file, which carries a _comment key recording why rule-em-dash is disabled.
evals.expected_output: The rationale key is reported as a documented annotation, not flagged as an unknown key. JSON has no comment syntax and the skill allows _comment in a legacy JSON file for exactly this purpose, so a config that records its reasoning is conforming. The skill also offers to carry the values into docs/conventions/ai-slop.yaml with the text as YAML comments.
expectations: Does NOT flag _comment as unknown-key drift
Still flags genuinely unknown keys in the same file, so the allowance is scoped to _comment rather than disabling the drift check
Surfaces the recorded rationale when reporting the disabled rule, so a reader sees why the exemption exists

evals.name: disabling-a-rule-records-its-reason
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup apply — user asks to disable rule-em-dash repo-wide because the house style uses em dashes deliberately.
evals.expected_output: The team-layer diff adds rule-em-dash to disabled_rules AND records the reason as a YAML comment above it, with the measured scale of the exemption named. The trade-off is stated plainly: disabling turns the rule off for new files too, where em_dash_allowed_paths would not.
expectations: Writes the reason alongside the exemption rather than the exemption alone
Names the trade-off between disabled_rules and em_dash_allowed_paths so the choice is informed
Does not change the plugin's shipped default — the exemption lives in the consuming repo's config only

evals.name: apply-moves-old-user-global-file
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup apply — ~/.claude/ai-slop.json sets vocab_add: ["synergy"], the repository has no docs/conventions/ai-slop.local.yaml, and docs/conventions/**/*.local.* is gitignored.
evals.expected_output: The skill names ~/.claude/ai-slop.json as an old path read in the personal layer's place, previews docs/conventions/ai-slop.local.yaml carrying vocab_add: [synergy], says the override applies only in this repository, and asks for a yes. After the yes it writes the override, re-runs --show-config to confirm vocab_add now resolves from the override, and only then deletes the old file.
expectations: Names the old file and the personal override as its new location before any write
Waits for an explicit yes before writing the override or deleting the old file
Re-runs --show-config and confirms the moved key resolves from docs/conventions/ai-slop.local.yaml before deleting ~/.claude/ai-slop.json
Does not add a userConfig option or write the team file for the moved settings
